responsibility: `rustc_passes` packages a collection of early and mid-level compiler analyses and validation passes over the crate’s AST and HIR, and exposes them to the rest of rustc through query providers registered by the crate root `lib.rs`, which declares the pass modules, loads the crate’s diagnostics, and assembles the single `provide` entry point. Its `errors.rs` file supplies the shared structured diagnostics used across these analyses. The crate validates source-level annotations and language constraints through passes such as `check_attr.rs`, which checks built-in and rustc attributes and provides module-attribute queries; `check_const.rs`, which enforces HIR-level restrictions for const contexts before MIR const checking; `loops.rs`, which verifies valid `break`/`continue` control flow; and `naked_functions.rs`, which enforces the rules for `#[naked]` functions and `naked_asm!`. It performs item and metadata collection needed by later compilation stages: `debugger_visualizer.rs` gathers crate debugger visualizer definitions; `diagnostic_items.rs` builds the mapping of diagnostic items; `lang_items.rs` collects and validates language items across the crate graph; `weak_lang_items.rs` checks required weak lang item availability; `lib_features.rs` extracts declared library features from stability attributes; `stability.rs` computes and validates stability, const-stability, and deprecation information; and `entry.rs` determines the crate entry function for executables. It also runs semantic analyses over program structure and usage: `dead.rs` implements dead-code analysis and related lints; `reachable.rs` computes which local definitions are externally reachable and therefore relevant for cross-crate use and codegen decisions; `upvars.rs` determines which outer locals closures capture; and `liveness.rs` provides the AST-based liveness analysis itself, with the `rustc_passes::liveness` module specifically managing the dense per-live-node, per-variable fact tables and efficient propagation operations that support that analysis. For compiler correctness and developer support, `hir_id_validator.rs` checks internal HIR ID consistency, `hir_stats.rs` reports AST/HIR size and count statistics, and `layout_test.rs` implements the internal `#[rustc_layout(...)]` testing pass that computes and reports type layout properties. Together, these modules make `rustc_passes` the crate responsible for a broad set of compiler passes that validate Rust items and attributes, collect semantic tables and special compiler metadata, analyze liveness, reachability, captures, and dead code, and provide the diagnostics and query results that later rustc stages depend on.
